MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
March 18, 2013

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m. on Monday,
March 18, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Councilmember Sanchez led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to the roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were
COUNCILMEMBERS: Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present
were City Manager Rock, Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community
Services Director McPherron, Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation
Director Harding, Administrative Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City Clerk
Shumway.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda.  Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada declared the month of April in 2013, as “Sexual Awareness Month,” and
specifically designated Monday, April 22, 2013, as “Denim Day.”

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that the City received a nine month permit
from the State of California Department of Public Health to operate the Cypress Water
Production Facility, and added that a letter will be sent to Lomita residents notifying them that
water blending will begin on April 1, 2013.

City Manager Rock informed City Council that federal legislators are looking to remove the
tax exemption status of municipal bonds as part of the efforts to deal with sequestration, and
added that staff would be bringing forward a resolution to the Council urging Congress to
continue supporting the tax exempt status of municipal bonds, and opposing any future
legislation to make changes related to this matter.

 5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE
  CITY COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina asked for clarification of the statement in the minutes that stated the
Railroad Museum Foundation would be taking control over the expenditures and revenues
related to the Railroad Museum Gift Shop, to which City Manager Rock replied that all Gift
Shop purchases would be made from funds of the Railroad Museum Foundation funds, not
from the City's General Fund, although the accounting for the Gift Shop would still be
performed by the City’s Administrative Services Department.

Councilmember Traina asked staff to consider using the best pavement materials for the
Eshelman Street Resurfacing Project, to which City Manager Rock responded that the award
for the construction of the Eshelman Street Resurfacing Project would be presented to City
Council at a future meeting.

Councilmember Savidan reported that he and Mayor Estrada attended a Meet and Greet
event for California State Assembly Member Al Muratsuchi. Councilmember Savidan also
stated that the Lomita Helicopter Noise Subcommittee members met with the United States
Coast Guard Commander regarding helicopter noise, and during the meeting they discussed
the possibility of modifying times and routes of training flights; as a result of the meeting and
recent efforts, residents have already seen some improvements.

Councilmember Gazeley, also serving as a Director of the Los Angeles Vector Control Board,
warned residents about the dangers of the West Nile Virus, and asked that they take
necessary precautions; Councilmember Gazeley went on to provide an overview of the
symptoms of West Nile Virus. As to the helicopter noise issue, Councilmember Gazeley
stated that the United States Coast Guard Commander cared about the problem and was
willing to work with Lomita officials to resolving it.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, inquired as to the cost of the Lomita newsletter, and whether
there was an increase in cost given the recent upgrades, such as the newsletter being
printed in color and on glossy paper. Furthermore, Ms. Segawa asked whether the City has
a texting policy, especially one concerning texting during working hours. Ms. Segawa also
expressed concern that the City Attorney was allowed to text during City Council meetings.

George Kivett, Executive Director of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, invited those in
attendance to the Chamber's next Business Mixer on Thursday, March 21, 2013, which will
take place at the Lomita Library, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. Mr. Kivett also invited those in
attendance to the Lomita Chamber's Breakfast on Friday, April 19, 2013, from 7:30 a.m. to 9
a.m., at which California State Assembly Member Al Muratsuchi will be a speaker.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez requested that Item 7.B be pulled from the Consent Agenda for
discussion, and Councilmember Traina requested that Item 7.E. be pulled from the Consent
Agenda for discussion.

  Page 2
 Regarding Item 7.B, Councilmember Sanchez requested clarification as to whether the
discussion of the appeal process of Planning Commission decisions would have to be
agendized under the Consent Agenda or the Regular Agenda, to which City Attorney Hogin
replied that staff would prepare a comparison of the appeal process with other jurisdictions,
place the matter on the Consent Agenda, and then later present the appeal process for
discussion at a public hearing.

Councilmember Traina stated that he pulled Item 7.E. from the Consent Agenda as he was
going to vote “no” on the item. Councilmember Sanchez stated that according to the staff
report minor savings would be seen as a result of the dissolution of the Tree Commission,
and asked to see what the savings would encompass, to which City Manager Rock replied
that the savings would mostly come from the elimination of overtime. Discussion followed
regarding the pros and cons of dissolving the Tree Commission. Councilmember Traina
expressed his concern as to whether the Parks and Recreation Commission had been made
aware of the added duties, and whether those Commissioners were willing to accept those
duties related to tree matters. Discussion continued on why only one extra responsibility had
been added to the Parks and Recreation Commission, and what was to happen with the
other duties of the Tree Commission. City Manager Rock clarified that in accordance with
the current Municipal Code, the majority of the duties related to the Tree Commission are
performed by the staff of the Public Works Department, therefore the Public Works Director
would decide as to what issues require public discussion, and in turn would place those
issues on the Parks and Recreation Commission agenda; routine matters would be
performed administratively.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Traina
seconded the motion.  The motion carried unanimously, with the exception of
Councilmembers Traina and Sanchez voting “NOES” on Item 7.E.

a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting held on

   PUBLIC HEARING

8. CAR2GO CAR SHARING PROGRAM AND MUNICIPAL CODE AMENDMENT
  ALLOWING CAR SHARING PARKING PERMIT ORDINANCE
Assistant City Manager Sugano provided an overview of the car2go car sharing program,
and added that a majority of cities in the South Bay need to agree to participate in the
program, and establish a permitting process, in order for the program to operate
successfully in the South Bay. According to Assistant City Manager Sugano, the City of
Lomita's participation includes allowing car2go vehicles to park in legal parking spaces
without regard to most time restrictions, except for restricted and posted parking of less than
one hour, as well as observing street sweeping restrictions and posted signs. Assistant City
Manager Sugano informed City Council that staff had negotiated a fee of $50 per vehicle,
per year, with car2go, as well as a $1,000 administrative fee to cover the cost of staff time
dealing with the permitting process and any possible complaints; it is currently estimated
that there will be up to 15 to 20 car2go vehicles in Lomita.
Councilmember Traina inquired as to what would happen if not all the cities in the South
Bay agree to participate in the car sharing program, and how that would affect Lomita, to
which Assistant City Manager Sugano responded that staff would still recommend
participating in the program, even if not all the cities in the South Bay agree to participate.
Councilmember Traina also asked whether staff anticipates more than one car sharing
business in the City of Lomita, and in turn how more than one car sharing business would
affect parking in Lomita. Assistant City Manager Sugano replied that the agreement is non-
exclusive, and that the same rules would apply to other companies.
Mayor Estrada stated that she was concerned about public safety, and asked whether staff
anticipates any complaints and how enforcement would be done. Assistant City Manager
Sugano responded that car2go will have a 24 hour / 7 day-a-week telephone number that
residents can call with issues, and added that car2go representatives assured City staff that
they would proactively respond to complaints, however, it is hard to currently anticipate how
many complaints would be received.
Discussion followed as to whether the City should put a cap on the number of car sharing
programs that could operate in the City, and the City could opt out of the agreement if too
many complaints are received. City Attorney Hogin stated that the agreement is for three
years, and that opting out or revoking the permit could only be done for cause.
Councilmember Gazeley emphasized that the sales tax will also be paid to the City, which
would be additional revenue.
Jackie Bacharach, Executive Director of the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG), stated that ca2go needs all nine cities in the South Bay to participate in the car
sharing program in order to have an economy to operate in. According to Ms. Bacharach,
SBCCOG's research of other jurisdictions that already have a similar program in place,
show that there are no complaints or issues with car sharing programs; SBCCOG supports
the car2go car sharing program. Ms. Bacharach also asked City Council to consider
modifying the motion to allow the City Manager to sign the agreement after a majority of, if
not all, the cities in the South Bay join the program.

  Page 4
 Walter Rosenkranz, car2go Consultant, stated that there will be a 24/7 call center that will
respond to concerns and complaints. According to Mr. Rosenkranz, in the whole City of
Seattle only five complaints have been received so far regarding the car2go car sharing
program.
George Kivett, Executive Director of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, stated that the
Lomita Chamber supports the car2go car sharing program, and that one of the benefits of
this program is that it will bring in sales tax revenue.
Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve staff’s recommendations, and also authorize the
City Manager to sign the agreement. City Attorney Hogin restated the motion: to adopt a
resolution agreeing to participate in the car2go program; introduce on first reading an
ordinance to amend the Municipal Code authorizing a parking permit process for car sharing
programs; and authorize the City Manager to sign the agreement. Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.
  SCHEDULED MATTERS

9. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF ADOPTING A RESOLUTION APPROVING
  THE CITY’S VISION, MISSION, AND CORE VALUES STATEMENTS

City Manager Rock informed City Council that on February 13, 2013, staff brought forward a
vision, mission, and core values for the City, which Council discussed and suggested some
possible changes; the proposed changes are incorporated in Attachment A of the staff
report.

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the vision statement suggested by
Councilmember Sanchez. Councilmembers Traina seconded the motion, which carried
unanimously.

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the mission statement as presented.
Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the core values as presented. Councilmember
Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

10. DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF CATCH BASIN BEST MANAGEMENT
  PRACTICES MACHADO LAKE TRASH TOTAL MAXIMUM DAILY LOAD (TMDL)
  CATCH BASIN RETROFIT

Public Works Director Damasse provided an overview of the staff report and stated that
according to the State of California Regional Water Quality Control Board, Los Angeles
Region, the level of trash discharging into Machado Lake currently violates the Board’s
water quality, thereby impairing beneficial uses. According to Director Damasse, Machado
Lake is the receiving body of urban and storm water water runoff from drainage systems
covering an approximately 20 square mile watershed, which includes the City of Lomita.
Director Damasse informed City Council that the City of Torrance has been agreed to serve
as the lead applicant for six cities in fabricating and installing more than 2,062 catch basin
inserts within partner cities' jurisdictions in order to prevent trash, leaves, and other debris

  Page 5
 from entering the drainage system. According to Director Damasse, implementation of this
project will bring the City into compliance with the requirements of the Clean Water Act for
the Machado Lake Watershed. Director Damasse also informed City Council that partner
cities are expected to contribute a 20% matching cost share, with the City of Lomita's share
being about $120,460. According to Director Damasse, the City of Lomita’s storm drain
system consists of approximately 277 catch basins, most of which are owned and operated
by the Los Angeles County Flood Control District (LACFCD). Given LACFCD's ownership
and operation of the catch basins, Director Damasse stated that this brings up the question
as to who is responsible for maintenance of the storm drains, which Director Damasse said
will be researched and brought back to Council at a future date.

Councilmember Traina stated that catch basins need screens to keep trash out, but that his
concern deals with the clogging of the catch basin screens and not allowing water to flow
through, to which Director Damasse replied that part of the program would also be
monitoring and maintenance of the catch basins.

Discussion followed as to whether the City should take ownership of the catch basins, or if
the County has to continue maintaining them. City Attorney Hogin clarified that this issue
deals with compliance with the Clean Water Act, and mainly concerns trash that comes from
city streets, which under the Clean Water Act, any party that contributes to the issue is
responsible for the trash, even if it made its way to the ocean through County operated
catch basins. Mayor Estrada added that in accordance with Proposition 84, there are fines
associated with trash not being cleaned out of catch basins.

Councilmember Traina again stated that he was primarily concerned with water not flowing
through the catch basins, and therefore stated that the City needed to have a plan to clean
the catch basins and maintain them on a regular basis.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, agreed with Councilmember Traina and stated that it will be
very problematic if the screening of the storm drains is increased, as there are some areas
that are historically subject to flooding. Mr. Kivett asked staff to be very proactive, especially
concerning the design of the catch basin screens and maintenance of the catch basins.
Councilmember Gazeley moved to accept the recommendations as presented by staff.
Councilmember Traina asked whether the City is going to address the possible liability to
personal property in the event that the storm drains do not collect water properly because of
the additional screening in the catch basins, to which City Attorney Hogin responded that in
general the City would not be liable if the city adheres to a reasonable method of
maintaining the catch basins.
City Manager Rock added that any such future liability claim would be reviewed on a case-
by-case basis. Councilmember Gazeley again moved to approve staff's recommendations.
Mayor Estrada seconded the motion.
Councilmember Traina requested that concerns about water flow and water backing up
because of the design of the catch basins be added to the motion, as Councilmember
Traina wanted this to be communicated to the County. City Manager Rock stated that
Councilmember Traina’s concerns would be reflected in the minutes.

  Page 6
 The motion carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 8:36 p.m.
